followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and any need for moderation-oriented handling.

On capability, this is a straightforward arithmetic word problem requiring multi-step reasoning. The benchmarks most predictive of that — MMLU-Pro, GPQA Diamond, and Arena-Hard — all favor Curlew by margins well above the 2.0-point variance threshold (79.6 vs 74.8, 61.8 vs 54.3, 88.4 vs 81.4). So Curlew is the stronger general-reasoning model in the fleet.

On the other axis, Whimbrel's distinguishing feature is its moderation-oriented post-training and flat preference response to harm-adjacent content. This query is completely benign, so that specialization offers no advantage here.

The task-preference data didn't drive the decision — those are self-reported preferences with no documented effect on output quality, so I don't treat them as quality signals. I went with the model that scores higher on the relevant capability evals for a clean reasoning task.
